# novig-docs

- [Novig Dev Docs](https://docs.novig.com/index.md): Get started with the NBX API
- [Authentication](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/authentication.md): OAuth 2.0 authentication for the NBX API
- [Data Model](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/data-model.md): Understanding how Novig structures events, markets, and outcomes
- [Understanding Outcome IDs](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/outcome-ids.md): How outcomes are organized and identified in the Novig API
- [Tick Table](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/ticks.md)
- [Trading Fees](https://docs.novig.com/fees.md): How Novig prices trading fees, and when they apply
- [Live Trading Maker Credit Program](https://docs.novig.com/maker-credit-program.md): Earn cash credits when your make order supplies liquidity: in-game on straight contracts, on every fill in NFL and NCAAF futures
- [Rate Limits & URL's](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/rest-api.md): HTTP REST API for order management and market data
- [Place order](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/orders/place-order.md): Place an order into the matching engine queue, conditional on validation. A successful response indicates that the order was placed in the queue, but does **not** guarantee that it will be filled or placed on the order book. To reliably ensure that an order has been executed, consume messages from t…
- [Place order batch](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/orders/place-order-batch.md): Submit multiple orders (maximum 256) at once to be processed in a batch. This operation does not make guarantees about the successful execution of all orders, it only places each in the matching engine queue.
- [Cancel order batch](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/orders/cancel-order-batch.md): Cancel up to 256 orders by ID. Each order must belong to the trader associated with the API key.
- [Get order](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/orders/get-order.md): Fetch details of a specific order using its unique identifier.
- [Cancel order](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/orders/cancel-order.md): Cancel a specific order by its unique identifier. The order must belong to the trader associated with the API key. This operation is idempotent, but does not make guarantees about reaching the matching engine before the order is filled. To reliably ensure that an order has been cancelled, consume me…
- [Cancel all orders](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/orders/cancel-all-orders.md): Cancel all active orders for the user, satisfying the provided parameters. This operation is idempotent, but does not make guarantees about reaching the matching engine before the orders are filled.
- [Get all my orders](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/orders/get-all-my-orders.md): Get a list of all orders associated with the user, satisfying the provided parameters. Results are limited to a maximum of 256 items per request (default 100).
- [Get all my fills](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/positions/get-all-my-fills.md): Access a complete list of all fills for the user, satisfying the provided parameters. This operation provides detailed records of each fill, including the quantity, price, and time of execution. Results are limited to a maximum of 256 items per request (default 100).
- [Get all my positions](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/positions/get-all-my-positions.md): Get a comprehensive overview of all positions held by the user, satisfying the provided parameters. This operation includes details about each position's size, entry price, and current market value. Results are limited to a maximum of 100 items by default.
- [Get market](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/markets/get-market.md): Fetch information for a specific market using its unique identifier.
- [Get open markets](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/markets/get-open-markets.md): Fetch a list of all markets currently open, satisfying the provided parameters.
- [Get order book](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/markets/get-order-book.md): Get the current order book for a specific market. For both outcomes of the market, orders are returned sorted by price-time priority. Orders on the book are partially obfuscated up to price, quantity, and direction.
- [Get markets by events (batch)](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/markets/get-markets-by-events-batch.md): Fetch markets for multiple events at once (maximum 50), including current orderbook data. Returns the same data as the single-event endpoint but in a single batched request.
- [Get markets by event](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/markets/get-markets-by-event.md): Fetch all markets for a specific event, including current orderbook data. This endpoint returns markets with their bid/ask data in a single response, eliminating the need to fetch orders separately.
- [Get lock status](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/markets/get-lock-status.md): Report every live trading lock: the current system lock, and the IDs of every locked event.
- [Request new market strike](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/markets/request-new-market-strike.md): Request a new strike for an existing market. This sends a notification to the Novig team, who may then choose to create the market. A successful response does **not** guarantee that the market will be created.
- [Get ticks](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/markets/get-ticks.md): Fetch the canonical set of valid submittable price ticks. Orders must be priced at one of these ticks; prices outside the table will be rejected.
- [Get leagues](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/events/get-leagues.md): Fetch a list of all available leagues.
- [Get event types](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/events/get-event-types.md): Fetch a list of all available event types.
- [Get event statuses](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/events/get-event-statuses.md): Fetch a list of all available event statuses.
- [Get events](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/events/get-events.md): Fetch a list of events with optional filters. Results are limited to a maximum of 100 items by default.
- [Get event](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/events/get-event.md): Fetch details of a specific event using its unique identifier.
- [Get wallet balance](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/account/get-wallet-balance.md): Get the current balance of the user's wallet under the given currency denomination.
- [Get open costs](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/account/get-open-costs.md): Get the user's open position cost and open order cost for the given currency denomination.
- [Get dashboard URL](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/account/get-dashboard-url.md): Issue a single-use, presigned URL to the EMM analytics dashboard for the authenticated trader.
- [Get user transactions](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/account/get-user-transactions.md): Get a detailed history of all transactions made by the user, satisfying the provided parameters. Results are limited to a maximum of 256 items per request (default 100).
- [WebSocket Overview](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/WSS/overview.md): Real-time market data and order updates via WebSocket
- [WebSocket Authentication](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/WSS/authentication.md): Authenticate WebSocket connections with JWT tokens
- [Order Book Channel](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/WSS/orderbook-channel.md): Subscribe to real-time order book updates
- [Market Lifecycle Channel](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/WSS/lifecycle-channel.md): Subscribe to market lifecycle events
- [Private Updates Channel](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/WSS/private-channel.md): Receive private fill and cancel notifications
- [Heartbeat & Connection Management](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/WSS/heartbeat.md): Keep WebSocket connections alive and handle reconnection
- [Code Example](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/WSS/code-examples.md)
- [GraphQL Overview](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/graphql/overview.md): Flexible querying API for market data and historical analysis
- [GraphQL Playground](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/graphql/playground.md): Interactive explorer for the Novig GraphQL API
- [Market Queries](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/graphql/market-queries.md): Query market data, outcomes, and order books
- [Player Queries](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/graphql/player-queries.md): Query player information, stats, and team rosters
- [RFQ Overview](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/rfq/overview.md): How Liquidity Providers respond to Novig parlay RFQs
- [RFQ Eligibility](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/rfq/eligibility.md): Which markets and leagues can appear together in a parlay RFQ
- [Parlay Settlement](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/rfq/settlement.md): How an executed RFQ parlay grades, and how its payout is computed
- [Registering Your Pricer](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/rfq/registration.md): Register your pricer webhook and verify it end-to-end, self-serve
- [Webhook Endpoints](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/rfq/webhooks.md): The /quote, /confirm, and /ping endpoints your pricer must implement
- [Webhook Signing](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/rfq/signing.md): Verifying X-Novig-Signature on inbound RFQ webhooks
- [Execution Feed & Reconciliation](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/rfq/executions.md): Watch RFQ executions live and reconcile the ones you won
- [Exchange Data](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/trade-data.md)
- [Affiliate Integration](https://docs.novig.com/affiliates/overview.md): Getting started with Novig affiliate partnerships
- [Deeplinking](https://docs.novig.com/affiliates/deeplinking.md): Direct users into the Novig app with pre-populated bet slips
- [Odds Screens](https://docs.novig.com/affiliates/odds-screens.md): Display Novig odds using our read-only GraphQL API
- [Parlay Pricing](https://docs.novig.com/affiliates/parlay-pricing.md): Query real-time Novig parlay prices within your UI
- [Futures Markets](https://docs.novig.com/affiliates/futures.md): Integrating Novig futures markets into your platform
- [API Changelog](https://docs.novig.com/api-reference/changelog.md): This changelog is specific to our API users and EMM's
